speaker: Sheldon
text: Count me out. You want me to use my intelligence in a tawdry competition? Would you ask Picasso to play Pictionary? Would you ask Noah Webster to play Boggle? Would you ask Jacques Cousteau to play Go Fish?

speaker: Raj
text: What? Come on, you need a four-person team. We're four people.

speaker: Sheldon
text: By that reasoning, we should also play bridge, hold up a hula hoop, and enter the Olympic bobsled competition.

speaker: Raj
text: There aren't tickets to that, please. Do I need to quote Spock's dying words to you? The needs of the many outweigh the needs of the few or the one.

speaker: Raj
text: Our whole universe was in a hot dense state, then nearly fourteen billion years ago, expansion started. Wait, the Earth began to cool, the autotrophs began to drool, Neanderthals developed tools, we built a wall.

speaker: Raj
text: We built the pyramids, math, science, history, unraveling the mystery that falls.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Okay. First order of physics, bold business. We need a truly kick-ass team name. Suggestions?

speaker: Raj
text: How about the perpetual motion squad? It's beyond the laws of physics, plus a little more something for the ladies. For the ladies? Perpetual motion squad. We can go all night.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I like it. I don't. Teams are traditionally named after fierce creatures, thus intimidating one's opponent.

speaker: Raj
text: Then we could be the Bengal tigers.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Poor choice. Yeah, gram for gram, no animal exceeds the relative fighting strength of the army ant. Maybe so.

speaker: Raj
text: But you can't incinerate a Bengal tiger with a magnifying glass.
